## 2. Solo Developer Strategy

### 2.1 Key Principles for Solo Success

1. **Quality Over Speed** - Better to ship later with great code than ship fast with tech debt
2. **Leverage Existing Tools** - Use libraries, templates, and no-code solutions wherever possible
3. **Focus on High-Value Features** - Prioritize P0 features, defer P2 until post-launch
4. **Sustainable Pace** - 45-50 hours/week is sustainable; don't burn out
5. **Automation First** - Automate testing, deployment, tedious tasks
6. **Document as You Go** - Solo means no pair programming; good docs = future you's best friend

### 2.2 Solo Developer Advantages

✅ **Decision Speed** - No meetings, no consensus needed  
✅ **Code Consistency** - One style, one architecture  
✅ **Full Ownership** - You know every line of code  
✅ **Learning Opportunity** - Full-stack experience across all layers  
✅ **Flexibility** - Adjust scope/timeline as you learn  

### 2.3 Solo Developer Challenges & Solutions

| Challenge | Solution |
|-----------|----------|
| Long hours on single features | Time-box each task, switch contexts frequently |
| Debugging alone | Comprehensive logging, rubber-duck debugging |
| Burnout risk | Strict 45-50h/week limit, weekends off |
| Limited peer review | Use linters, automated tests, code quality tools |
| Context switching costs | Group similar tasks in blocks |
| Single point of failure | Good documentation, version control, backups |

### 2.4 Weekly Structure (Solo)

**Example Week Schedule:**

| Day | Time | Activity |
|-----|------|----------|
| **Mon** | 9-12:30 (3.5h) | Planning, architecture decisions, PR reviews of own work |
| **Mon** | 1-5 (4h) | Deep work on Phase task |
| **Tue-Thu** | 9-1 (4h) | Feature development |
| **Tue-Thu** | 2-6 (4h) | Feature development (40h total/week) |
| **Fri** | 9-1 (4h) | Testing, documentation |
| **Fri** | 2-4 (2h) | Weekly retrospective, planning next week |
| **Total** | ~50h | Sustainable, focused work |

## 10. Dependencies & Critical Path

### 10.1 Critical Path Analysis

```
Phase 1 (Complete) ──▶ Phase 2 (Infrastructure) ──▶ Phase 3 (AI) ──┬──▶ Phase 4 (RAG)
                                                                      │
                                                                      └──▶ Phase 5 (Personalization)
                                                                            │
                                                                            ▼
                                                                      Phase 6 (Launch)
```

### 10.2 Inter-Phase Dependencies

| Phase | Blocking Dependencies | Can Start If |
|-------|----------------------|--------------|
| Phase 2 | Phase 1 complete | Foundation docs approved |
| Phase 3 | Phase 2 complete | Auth + DB + UI foundation ready |
| Phase 4 | Phase 3 complete | Chat interface functional |
| Phase 5 | Phase 4 complete (partial) | RAG working, can parallelize UI |
| Phase 6 | Phase 5 complete | All features implemented |

### 10.3 Work Sequencing (Solo)

**Week 3-4 (Phase 2):**
- Build frontend and backend in sequence (or overlap where possible)
- Start auth after the DB schema is defined

**Week 5-6 (Phase 3):**
- Develop AI integration and chat UI together
- Add conversation persistence once the DB is ready

**Week 7-8 (Phase 4):**
- Document processing and vector setup can overlap
- Upload UI can start early with a mocked API

**Week 9-10 (Phase 5):**
- Settings UI and backend config can be built in parallel slices

## 11. Risk Mitigation Strategies (Solo Developer)

### 11.1 Technical Risks

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation Strategy |
|------|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| **AI SDK 6 Beta breaking changes** | High | Medium | Pin specific versions, monitor changelog, maintain v5 fallback, subscribe to release notes |
| **Prisma 7 migration issues** | High | Medium | Test migrations on staging first, maintain rollback scripts, review docs thoroughly |
| **LLM rate limiting (Groq)** | High | Medium | Implement retry logic with exponential backoff, monitor usage, request quota increases early |
| **Vector search performance degradation** | Medium | Low | Monitor latency continuously, optimize chunk size, add caching layer (Redis optional) |
| **Document processing failures** | Medium | Medium | Add robust error handling, retry mechanism, detailed status tracking, test with various doc types |
| **Auth.js v5 session issues** | High | Low | Thoroughly test auth flows early, follow official examples, use next-auth testing utilities |
| **Database schema issues** | High | Low | Carefully design schema upfront, test migrations, keep migration history |

### 11.2 Schedule Risks

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation Strategy |
|------|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| **Phase overruns** | High | Medium | Build 1-week buffer into each phase (extra 6 weeks available), don't scope-creep, stick to PRD |
| **Context switching delays** | High | High | Block out 4-hour focus time daily, batch similar tasks, minimize context switches |
| **Burnout from sustained 50h/week** | Critical | High | **Maintain strict 40-50h/week limit**, take weekends completely off, track energy levels |
| **Single developer illness/emergency** | Critical | Low | Document everything, keep code quality high, maintain git history, automated tests |
| **Dependency delays (third-party APIs)** | Medium | Medium | Build fallback implementations, test with vendor libraries early, have contingency plans |
| **Scope creep (P2 features)** | High | Medium | Lock PRD, say "no" to new features, defer P2 items until post-launch |

### 11.3 Quality Risks

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation Strategy |
|------|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| **Insufficient testing (no time)** | High | High | **Write tests as you code**, aim for 60%+ coverage, automate in CI/CD, prioritize critical paths |
| **Code quality issues (tired developer)** | Medium | Medium | Use ESLint/TypeScript strictly, code reviews (self-review), refactor during Phase 6 |
| **Security vulnerabilities** | Critical | Low | Security audit in Phase 6, use OWASP checklist, validate all inputs with Zod, avoid custom auth |
| **Performance degradation** | Medium | Medium | Monitor with Lighthouse regularly, test on slow networks, profile during development |
| **Poor UX from developer perspective only** | Medium | Medium | Ask for feedback mid-project, use design frameworks (shadcn/ui), follow accessibility standards |

### 11.4 Resource & Budget Risks

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation Strategy |
|------|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| **API cost overruns (Groq, Upstash, Vercel)** | Medium | High | Set spending alerts on all services, monitor usage weekly, implement rate limiting early |
| **Database storage costs** | Low | Low | Monitor growth, implement cleanup strategies, archive old documents |
| **Upstash Vector limits** | Medium | Low | Monitor namespace usage, test scaling early, have quota increase plan |
| **Tool license costs** | Low | Medium | Use free tiers (GitHub, Vercel free, Groq API), avoid paid tools unnecessarily |

### 11.5 Mental Health & Sustainability Risks

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation Strategy |
|------|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| **Burnout from isolation** | High | High | **Weekly progress celebration**, social interaction, work with others (pair programming optional) |
| **Decision paralysis** | Medium | High | Make decisions quickly, document rationale, avoid perfectionism, iterate instead of perfect-first |
| **Imposter syndrome** | Medium | High | Celebrate wins daily, track progress, remember: this is a real, complex project |
| **Lack of motivation in Phase 5-6** | Medium | High | Plan celebration for major milestones, break into smaller wins, visualize launch day |

## 12. Quality Assurance Plan (Solo Developer)

### 12.1 Solo Developer Testing Philosophy

As a solo developer, you can't afford to waste time on tests that don't matter. Focus on:
- ✅ **High-risk areas:** Auth, RAG retrieval, API endpoints
- ✅ **UI critical path:** Auth → Chat → Settings
- ✅ **Integration points:** API → DB, LLM calls, Vector search
- ❌ **Skip:** Trivial component tests, snapshot tests (brittle), 100% coverage goal

**Target:** 60%+ coverage on critical code paths. Don't aim for 100%.

### 12.2 Testing Strategy (Practical)

| Phase | What to Test | Tools | How Much Time |
|-------|--------------|-------|--------------|
| **As You Code** | Write tests for API endpoints | Jest, Supertest | 10% of coding time |
| **As You Code** | Test critical libraries locally | Manual + Jest | 5% of coding time |
| **Phase 6, Week 15** | Component unit tests | React Testing Library | 15 hours |
| **Phase 6, Week 16** | Integration tests (API flows) | Jest | 12 hours |
| **Phase 6, Week 16** | E2E tests (critical user paths) | Playwright | 10 hours |
| **Phase 6, Week 18** | Manual QA & exploratory | Manual testing | 8 hours |
| **Continuous** | Run tests in CI/CD | GitHub Actions | Automatic |

### 12.3 Code Review Process (Solo)

**Your Code Review Checklist (use before committing):**

1. **Does it work?**
   - ✅ Tested locally?
   - ✅ Handles errors gracefully?
   - ✅ Works on slow networks?

2. **Is it clean?**
   - ✅ No console.logs?
   - ✅ No commented-out code?
   - ✅ TypeScript no errors?
   - ✅ ESLint passing?

3. **Is it maintainable?**
   - ✅ Function < 30 lines?
   - ✅ Variable names clear?
   - ✅ Complex logic documented?

4. **Is it safe?**
   - ✅ User inputs validated?
   - ✅ No hardcoded secrets?
   - ✅ No SQL injection risk?

### 12.4 Definition of Done (Solo)

A feature is done when:
- ✅ Code written and committed
- ✅ Tested locally (manual or unit tests)
- ✅ TypeScript and ESLint pass
- ✅ Self-reviewed before commit
- ✅ Deployed to preview environment
- ✅ Manual testing passed
- ✅ Acceptance criteria met

### 12.5 Debugging Strategy (Working Alone)

When stuck:
1. **Rubber duck debugging:** Explain problem to a rubber duck (or blog post)
2. **Sleep on it:** Often solutions come after rest
3. **Isolate:** Create minimal reproduction
4. **Search:** Google error message + tech stack
5. **Console.log:** Strategically log state before/after
6. **Debugger:** Use VS Code debugger for breakpoints
7. **Pair programming:** Ask for help (optional async pair session)

## 13. Solo Developer Workflows & Productivity

### 13.1 Daily Standup (Solo Edition)

You're your own manager. Try this daily routine:

**Morning (9:00 AM, 15 min)**
- Review yesterday's commit log  
- Check GitHub issues/PRs if any
- Set top 3 priorities for today
- Note any blockers

**End of Day (5:00 PM, 10 min)**
- Commit code with clear messages
- Update progress tracking (e.g., notion, linear, github projects)
- Plan tomorrow
- Celebrate 1 win from today

### 13.2 Weekly Rhythm

| Day | Focus | Time |
|-----|-------|------|
| **Monday Afternoon** | Plan the week, review blockers from last week | 1h |
| **Tue-Thu Mornings** | Deep work on features (minimize distractions) | 4h each |
| **Tue-Thu Afternoons** | Bug fixes, minor tasks, code review | 3h each |
| **Friday Morning** | Weekly retrospective: what worked? what didn't? | 1h |
| **Friday Afternoon** | Polish code, document progress, prepare next week | 2h |

### 13.3 Tools for Solo Productivity

**Essential:**
- GitHub Issues or Linear: Track tasks
- VS Code: Main editor
- GitHub Projects: Visual task board (free)
- Notion or Obsidian: Technical notes (optional)

**Nice to Have:**
- Toggl Track: Time tracking (optional)
- Slack: Accountability messaging (optional)
- Discord: Community support (join dev communities)

### 13.4 Documentation Standard (Solo)

Write this as you go (don't leave until end):
- **Code comments:** For "why", not "what"
- **README:** Update with new features/scripts
- **Architecture decisions:** Quick notes in ADR format (optional)
- **Setup guide:** Tested by running `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` and verifying everything works

### 13.5 Mental Health as a Solo Developer

**Build in wins:**
- Ship a feature every 2-3 days
- Celebrate small milestones
- Track burndown (what % complete?)
- Take real breaks (not "break by coding another language")

**Fight isolation:**
- Weekly async pair programming session (optional)
- Join dev communities (Dev.to, Indie Hackers)
- Share progress publicly (Twitter, Discord, blog)
- Get feedback: share designs/code with someone

**Prevent burnout:**
- ⏰ **Strict cutoff:** Stop at 50h/week, period
- 📅 **Weekends off:** No coding Saturday/Sunday
- 🏃 **Exercise:** Non-negotiable, 3x/week
- 😴 **Sleep:** 8 hours minimum
- 🤝 **Social:** Time with friends/family

## 14. Success Metrics & KPIs (Solo Developer)

### 14.1 Development Metrics

**Measure these weekly during development:**

| Metric | Target | How to Measure | Action if Miss |
|--------|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Lines of Code per Week** | 800-1500 LOC/week | `git log --oneline` count | Normal; quality > quantity |
| **Commits per Week** | 15-25 commits | GitHub commit history | Aim for small, logical commits |
| **Stalled Issues** | 0 blockers > 1 day | GitHub issues | Remove blocker immediately |
| **Code Quality** | 0 TypeScript errors | `npm run typecheck` | Fix all TS errors daily |
| **Test Coverage** | 60%+ by Phase 6 | Jest coverage report | Add tests if < 60% |
| **CI/CD Pass Rate** | 100% | GitHub Actions | Fix failing tests before merge |

### 14.2 Velocity Metrics (How fast are you going?)

**Track progress weekly:**

| Week | Phase | Target Hours | Actual Hours | Notes |
|------|-------|--------------|--------------|-------|
| Week 3 | Phase 2 | 39h | ___ | Track your actual pace |
| Week 4 | Phase 2 | 46h | ___ | Is 50h/week sustainable? |
| Week 5 | Phase 2 | 45h | ___ | Adjust estimate if needed |
| Week 6-8 | Phase 3 | 45-48h | ___ | Maintaining velocity? |
| Week 9-12 | Phase 4 | 47-48h | ___ | Complex phase; watch pace |
| Week 13-14 | Phase 5 | 45-48h | ___ | Maintaining?  (Possible dip here?) |
| Week 15-18 | Phase 6 | 50h | ___ | Final push to launch |

**Action:** If you're not hitting hours target, either:
- Task estimates are too optimistic (adjust Phase 6)
- You're doing extra work (stay focused on PRD)
- You need better focus time (more 4h blocks)

### 14.3 Feature Completion Metrics

**Track monthly to see progress:**

| Feature | Phase | Status | Launch Blocking? |
|---------|-------|--------|------------------|
| Core Infrastructure | 2 | ✅ | P0 |
| Chat Interface | 3 | 🔄 | P0 |
| Document Upload | 4 | ⏳ | P0 |
| RAG Retrieval | 4 | ⏳ | P0 |
| Settings/Personalization | 5 | ⏳ | P1 |
| Testing & Polish | 6 | ⏳ | P0 |

### 14.4 Technical Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| **Chat Response Latency** | < 3s | Custom logging in API |
| **Document Processing** | < 30s/MB | Server-side timing |
| **Vector Search** | < 100ms | Upstash latency |
| **Lighthouse Score** | > 90 | Lighthouse CI |
| **API Uptime** | 99%+ | Uptime monitoring |
| **Error Rate** | < 1% | Sentry tracking |

### 14.5 Sustainability Metrics (Most Important!)

**You succeed if you launch healthy, not burned out:**

| Metric | Target | How to Measure | Red Flag |
|--------|--------|----------------|----------|
| **Weekly Hours** | 45-50h | Time tracking | > 55h = burnout risk |
| **Code Quality** | No urgent fixes | Happy with your code? | Dreading code reviews |
| **Sleep** | 8 hours/night | Sleep tracking | < 7h consistently |
| **Motivation** | 8/10+ | Self-rating daily | < 6/10 for 3+ days |
| **Progress Satisfaction** | 8/10+ | Weekly reflection | Feeling stuck? |
| **Social Life** | Still has friends! | Meeting friends weekly | Isolated/alone? |

**RED FLAGS - Act immediately:**
- Working > 55h/week consistently
- Sleeping < 7 hours regularly
- Motivation drops below 6/10
- Feeling isolated or lonely
- Code quality suffering (can't debug your own code)
- Physical symptoms (headaches, stress)

**If you see RED FLAGS:**
1. Talk to someone (friend, mentor, therapist)
2. Reduce scope (defer Phase 5 personalization until post-launch)
3. Extend timeline (Phase 6 extended another month?)
4. Break up large tasks into smaller wins

### 14.6 Post-Launch Success Metrics

**After you go live (starting June 3, 2026):**

| Metric | Target | Measurement |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| **App Availability** | 99.5%+ | Uptime monitoring |
| **Chat Completion Rate** | > 80% | User analytics |
| **Document Indexing Success** | > 95% | Error tracking |
| **User Retention (Week 1)** | 70%+ | Analytics |
| **Response Time (p95)** | < 3s | Server-side monitoring |
| **No Critical Bugs** | 0 in first week | Sentry + manual checks |
| **User Satisfaction** | Positive feedback | Comments/reviews |

### 14.7 Personal Success

**You've succeeded if, on launch day, you can say:**

- ✅ "I shipped on time (June 2 or close)"
- ✅ "Code quality is professional and maintainable"
- ✅ "I'm not burned out"
- ✅ "Features work reliably"
- ✅ "I'm proud of what I built"
- ✅ "Users can actually use the product"

**Final measure of success:** Can you hand this off to someone else and they can maintain/extend it?

## Appendix C: Tools & Technology Checklist

### Required Accounts (Set up Week 1-2)

- [ ] GitHub account + new repo
- [ ] Vercel account (connected to GitHub)
- [ ] Vercel Postgres database created
- [ ] Groq account + API key
- [ ] Upstash Vector account + API keys
- [ ] Google Cloud Console + OAuth credentials
- [ ] Email or Discord for notifications

### Development Tools (Install Week 1-2)

```bash
# System
node --version  # v20+
npm install -g pnpm  # Package manager

# Project setup
pnpm install  # All dependencies
pnpm prisma migrate dev  # Database
pnpm dev  # Start dev server

# Code quality
pnpm typecheck  # TypeScript check
pnpm lint  # ESLint
pnpm test  # Jest tests (Phase 6)
```

### Recommended VS Code Extensions

- **Prisma** (prisma.prisma) - Schema editing
- **ESLint** (dbaeumer.vscode-eslint) - Linting
- **Prettier** (esbenp.prettier-vscode) - Formatting
- **Thunder Client** or **REST Client** - API testing
- **GitHub Copilot** (optional) - Code assistance
- **GitLens** (eamodio.gitlens) - Git history

### Free Services Used

| Service | Purpose | Free Tier | Cost |
|---------|---------|------------|------|
| **GitHub** | Version control, CI/CD | Unlimited public/private repos | $0 |
| **Vercel** | Hosting + Postgres | 90 serverless function minutes | $0 |
| **Groq** | LLM API | 30 req/min, 100 req/day | $0 pay-as-you-go |
| **Upstash** | Vector DB | 28 days free, then $0.25/day | $0-$10/month |
| **Google Cloud** | OAuth | Free tier | $0 |

**Total estimated cost:** $0-$50/month during development

## Appendix E: Critical Success Factors

**These are non-negotiable:**

1. **Protect your time:** 45-50h/week, not 70+h
2. **Keep scope tight:** P0 + P1 only, defer P2 until launch successful
3. **Automate testing:** Don't test manually each time, use CI/CD
4. **Document as you go:** Future you will thank you
5. **Celebrate wins:** Ship features every 1-2 weeks
6. **Watch for burnout:** Red flags section in Section 14
7. **Get feedback early:** Share designs/code with someone
8. **Ship minimum viable:** Don't over-engineer (iterate post-launch)

**Most important:** You can have a great product OR work 80 hours/week. Not both. Choose the great product + sustainable pace.
